findings.evidence: Glob of `RoughCoefficients/` lists both `HigherOrder.lean` (qualitative `memWkpLoc_succ`, `apply_I_of_hasWeakFDerivOn`) and the new `HigherOrderEstimate.lean` (the quantitative version of that same induction).
findings.fix: `git mv` `RoughCoefficients/HigherOrder.lean` to `RoughCoefficients/HigherOrder/Basic.lean`, put the new file at `RoughCoefficients/HigherOrder/Estimate.lean`, and update the imports.
findings.issue: The new file creates `HigherOrder.lean` and `HigherOrderEstimate.lean` as flat siblings sharing the subject 'HigherOrder' (higher-order interior regularity).

findings.evidence: Its proof uses only `eLpNormWkp_clm_comp_le (apply ℝ F v)` plus an operator-norm bound, the same pattern as `eLpNormWkp_neg_le`, which this PR adds to `Norm.lean`. It has no CR hypotheses.
findings.fix: Make it public in `TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/Local/Norm.lean`, next to `eLpNormWkp_clm_comp_le` and the new `eLpNormWkp_neg_le`.
findings.issue: `private eLpNormWkp_apply_le` (evaluating a field of linear maps at a vector with ‖v‖ ≤ 1 does not increase the W^{k,p} norm) is a generic Sobolev-norm fact hidden in a CR-specific file.

findings.evidence: `Coordinates.lean:140` has `memWkpLoc_succ_iff_apply_one_apply_I`, the qualitative counterpart. `Norm.lean:91` has `eLpNormWkp_succ_le`, which this lemma refines.
findings.fix: Make it public in `TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/Local/Coordinates.lean`, next to `memWkpLoc_succ_iff_apply_one_apply_I` (or in `Norm.lean` beside `eLpNormWkp_succ_le`).
findings.issue: `private eLpNormWkp_succ_succ_le` (W^{k+2,q} norm bounded by the L^q norm and the W^{k+1,q} norms of ∂_s u and ∂_t u) is a generic Sobolev lemma on ℂ, not CR material.

summary: The new estimate file sits flat next to its sibling `HigherOrder.lean` instead of the two being grouped in a `HigherOrder/` directory. Two generic Sobolev-norm lemmas are kept `private` inside the Cauchy–Riemann file instead of living in the Sobolev library.
